content.comment_body: Hi, I would like to measure water and gas (Actaris G4) consumption using the hall sensor mentioned above. I saw on another forum that this should be possible. I have a [product_name] [article_no] connected to KNX and need advice on wiring the hall sensor to it. My electronics knowledge is limited, so any assistance would be appreciated. Thanks!

The [product_name] has two analog inputs, but both are 0-10V. Reviewing the datasheet for your sensor, it appears to work in a different range. I think you would need some sort of analog converter, as direct connection is not possible.
Since the sensor provides a switch output, you can use it as a counter input for the [product_name]. Check page 3 of the datasheet for details.

Your hall sensor functions as a switch rather than a typical sensor. You can wire it directly to the digital input on your [product_name]. Apply the same voltage to both the switch and the [product_name], either 24 VDC or 12 VDC, depending on your setup. Best of luck.

Thanks, [user_name]. Could you clarify the physical connections? I assume pin 1 of the sensor should connect to the power supply on the [product_name], pin 3 to a digital input, but where should the ground wire go? Many thanks!

analysis.insight_summary: Community members are sharing advice on how to connect a hall sensor to a [product_name] controller for monitoring utility consumption. There's initial uncertainty over input compatibility, but users clarify that the sensor acts as a switch and can be connected directly to digital inputs. An important user insight is the need for clear guides or documentation for connecting third-party sensors to [product_name], especially for those with limited electronics experience.
